north_star: Any person or agent can turn an unfamiliar displayed phone number into a country-aware, source-backed caller-campaign answer, take a concrete safety action, and privately monitor material changes.
wedge: One shared lookup and caller-campaign contract across CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web, starting with official NL, GB, and US evidence and expanding through controlled first-party reports, private watches, verified organisation declarations, corpus transparency, and hosted MCP.
target_user: People checking unfamiliar calls, AI agents, and developers building safety-conscious unknown-caller experiences.
core_promise: Normalize once, check eligible country-aware evidence, explain the calibrated campaign risk and uncertainty, and offer a safe next action without guessing identity or safety.
product_principles: Displayed number is evidence context, never proof of caller identity, guilt, reachability, or safety.
Every result uses one of four calibrated risk states: official_warning, elevated_signals, no_risk_evidence, or insufficient_evidence.
No risk evidence requires at least one current, eligible, risk-capable source to have been checked without a match; it never means safe.
Only official, explicitly licensed, or first-party moderated evidence can influence reputation; lookup demand cannot.
Every conclusion carries provenance, freshness, confidence, reasons, gaps, and a plain-language next action.
Machine-readable contracts lead; CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web render the same truth.
Caller campaigns are the durable risk object; membership describes calls displaying bounded values and never proves who called.
Monitoring is private, verified, revocable, minimized, and triggered only by material state changes.
Verified organisation portfolios prove a declaration of an official contact route, never the origin of a displayed call.
non_goals: Expose private subscriber identities, contact-book data, call histories, or requester identities.
Claim that a valid number is assigned, reachable, safe, dangerous, or owned by a named person without eligible evidence.
Scrape, copy, or republish third-party caller-report data without documented authority and reuse rights.
Treat lookup volume, virality, or one unverified report as reputation evidence.
Accept public reports before privacy, moderation, retention, correction, deletion, appeal, and abuse controls are approved and tested.
assumptions: Authoritative numbering-allocation data is lawfully reusable for at least the Netherlands, United Kingdom, and United States.
An explicit origin region is available whenever an input lacks an international country code.
Agents and developers value a prominent but calibrated risk state over either an unsupported identity guess or a dense evidence dump.
Third-party caller-report data is unavailable for ingestion unless a source registry entry documents explicit permission or a compatible licence.
First-party reporting can be introduced only after legal, privacy, moderation, retention, correction, deletion, appeal, and anti-brigading controls are approved and tested.
Phone-number portability and spoofing prevent allocation or report data from proving current provider, subscriber, or caller identity.
Users will opt into private monitoring when notifications are sparse, material, and easy to revoke.
Organisations can complete a bounded challenge workflow without that verification being misread as caller-origin proof.
success_metrics: A fresh clone validates all repository and .go contracts with one documented command.
CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web expose the same four-state risk contract and reason codes.
Every published assessment can be traced to eligible timestamped evidence and an explicit next action.
Every enabled source passes a machine-validated rights, provenance, freshness, permitted-fields, and outage gate.
Desktop and mobile results make the risk state more prominent than source confidence without calling an evidence-free number safe.
Every active campaign is schema-valid, freshness-bounded, correction-aware, and traceable to eligible independent evidence.
Private watches and verified organisation declarations pass consent, anti-enumeration, expiry, revocation, correction, and deletion tests.
Public corpus metrics explain actual coverage, freshness, moderation thresholds, and gaps without using lookup popularity as risk evidence.
